review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

9:1.sourceText: Καὶ παράγων εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον τυφλὸν ἐκ γενετῆς.
9:1.targetText: Now as Jesus was passing by, He saw a man blind from birth,

groups.note: The participle παράγων ("passing by") supplies the as-clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the participle.

9:2.sourceText: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Ῥαββεί, τίς ἥμαρτεν, οὗτος ἢ οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ, ἵνα τυφλὸς γεννηθῇ;
9:2.targetText: and His disciples asked Him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”

groups.note: Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is not rendered; English introduces the question directly.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:3.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Οὔτε οὗτος ἥμαρτεν οὔτε οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ, ἀλλ’ ἵνα φανερωθῇ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ.
9:3.targetText: Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the main clause that the Greek leaves implicit after ἀλλ’ ἵνα ("but so that").

9:4.sourceText: ἡμᾶς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ πέμψαντός με ἕως ἡμέρα ἐστίν· ἔρχεται νὺξ ὅτε οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐργάζεσθαι.
9:4.targetText: While it is daytime, we must do the works of Him who sent Me. Night is coming, when no one can work.

groups.note: The article with the participle ("of the one who sent") is rendered of Him who sent.

9:5.sourceText: ὅταν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ὦ, φῶς εἰμι τοῦ κόσμου.
9:5.targetText: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an article before light; φῶς has none here.

9:6.sourceText: ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἔπτυσεν χαμαὶ καὶ ἐποίησεν πηλὸν ἐκ τοῦ πτύσματος, καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτοῦ τὸν πηλὸν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς,
9:6.targetText: When Jesus had said this, He spit on the ground, made some mud, and applied it to the man’s eyes.

groups.note: BSB's Greek text differs at this word; applied also fits N1904's ἐπέθηκεν ("put on").
αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered the man’s.
τὸν πηλόν ("the mud") is rendered by the pronoun it.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lists the actions with a comma here; this καί has no separate English word.
BSB does not render ἐκ τοῦ πτύσματος ("from the saliva"); it says only made some mud.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the participle.

9:7.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ὕπαγε νίψαι εἰς τὴν κολυμβήθραν τοῦ Σιλωάμ (ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται Ἀπεσταλμένος). ἀπῆλθεν οὖν καὶ ἐνίψατο, καὶ ἦλθεν βλέπων.
9:7.targetText: Then He told him, “Go, wash in the Pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So the man went and washed, and came back seeing.

groups.note: With the indeclinable name Σιλωάμ, the article shows the genitive.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb.

9:8.sourceText: Οἱ οὖν γείτονες καὶ οἱ θεωροῦντες αὐτὸν τὸ πρότερον, ὅτι προσαίτης ἦν, ἔλεγον Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ καθήμενος καὶ προσαιτῶν;
9:8.targetText: At this, his neighbors and those who had formerly seen him begging began to ask, “Isn’t this the man who used to sit and beg?”

groups.note: The article with the participle ("those seeing") is rendered those who had seen.
τὸ πρότερον ("the former time") is rendered formerly.
ὅτι προσαίτης ἦν ("that he was a beggar") is rendered begging.
Οὐχ … ἐστιν ("is not") together form the contraction.
The article with the participle ("the one sitting") is rendered the man who used to sit.

9:9.sourceText: ἄλλοι ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν· ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Οὐχί, ἀλλὰ ὅμοιος αὐτῷ ἐστιν. ἐκεῖνος ἔλεγεν ὅτι Ἐγώ εἰμι.
9:9.targetText: Some claimed that he was, but others said, “No, he just looks like him.”  But the man kept saying, “I am the one.”

groups.note: ἐκεῖνος ("that one") is rendered the man.

unmappedSource.reason: ἀλλά ("but rather") after No has no English word; BSB states the correction directly.
The ὅτι introducing the quotation is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a contrast; the Greek has no connective here.
English adds just ("merely"); the Greek says only ὅμοιος αὐτῷ ἐστιν ("he is like him").
English adds a contrast; the Greek has no connective here.
English supplies the predicate left implicit in Ἐγώ εἰμι ("I am [he]").

9:10.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ Πῶς οὖν ἠνεῴχθησάν σου οἱ ὀφθαλμοί;
9:10.targetText: “How then were your eyes opened?” they asked.

unmappedSource.reason: The narrative οὖν ("so") is not rendered; BSB keeps only the then of the question.
The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:11.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος Ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰησοῦς πηλὸν ἐποίησεν καὶ ἐπέχρισέν μου τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς καὶ εἶπέν μοι ὅτι Ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν Σιλωὰμ καὶ νίψαι· ἀπελθὼν οὖν καὶ νιψάμενος ἀνέβλεψα.
9:11.targetText: He answered, “The man they call Jesus made some mud and anointed my eyes, and He told me to go to Siloam and wash. So I went and washed and received my sight.”

groups.note: ὁ λεγόμενος ("the one called") is rendered they call.
BSB turns the command Ὕπαγε ("Go") into indirect speech.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The ὅτι introducing the quotation is not rendered; BSB uses indirect speech.

unmappedTarget.reason: English and joins the participle clause to the main verb.

9:12.sourceText: καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ποῦ ἐστιν ἐκεῖνος; λέγει Οὐκ οἶδα.
9:12.targetText: “Where is He?” they asked.  “I do not know,” he answered.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί is not rendered; BSB starts with the question.
The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to him") is not rendered.

9:13.sourceText: Ἄγουσιν αὐτὸν πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους, τόν ποτε τυφλόν.
9:13.targetText: They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been blind.

groups.note: ποτε ("once, formerly") is expressed by the English had been.

9:14.sourceText: ἦν δὲ σάββατον ἐν ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ τὸν πηλὸν ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἀνέῳξεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς.
9:14.targetText: Now the day on which Jesus had made the mud and opened his eyes was a Sabbath.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an article before day; ἡμέρᾳ has none.

9:15.sourceText: πάλιν οὖν ἠρώτων αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πῶς ἀνέβλεψεν. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πηλὸν ἐπέθηκέν μου ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς, καὶ ἐνιψάμην, καὶ βλέπω.
9:15.targetText: So the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight.  The man answered, “He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and now I can see.”

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he; BSB says the man.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves πάλιν ("again") untranslated.
BSB does not render δέ here; it starts a new sentence.
The indirect object αὐτοῖς ("to them") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds now to mark the change; the Greek has the plain present βλέπω ("I see").

9:16.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων τινές Οὐκ ἔστιν οὗτος παρὰ Θεοῦ ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὅτι τὸ σάββατον οὐ τηρεῖ. ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Πῶς δύναται ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλὸς τοιαῦτα σημεῖα ποιεῖν; καὶ σχίσμα ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς.
9:16.targetText: Because of this, some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, for He does not keep the Sabbath.”  But others said, “How can a sinful man perform such signs?”  And there was division among them.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB's But follows a reading with an extra word here; N1904 has no connective before others.

9:17.sourceText: λέγουσιν οὖν τῷ τυφλῷ πάλιν Τί σὺ λέγεις περὶ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἠνέῳξέν σου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν ὅτι Προφήτης ἐστίν.
9:17.targetText: So once again they asked the man who had been blind, “What do you say about Him, since it was your eyes He opened?”  “He is a prophet,” the man replied.

groups.note: τῷ τυφλῷ ("the blind one") is rendered the man who had been blind.
In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he; BSB says the man.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render δέ here; the reply follows directly.
The ὅτι introducing the quotation is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English uses a cleft ("it was your eyes He opened"); the Greek has no such words.

9:18.sourceText: οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἦν τυφλὸς καὶ ἀνέβλεψεν, ἕως ὅτου ἐφώνησαν τοὺς γονεῖς αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἀναβλέψαντος
9:18.targetText: The Jews still did not believe that the man had been blind and had received his sight until they summoned his parents

groups.note: αὐτοῦ ("him") is rendered the man.
ἀνέβλεψεν ("he regained sight") is rendered had received his sight.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render οὖν ("so") here.
περί ("about") is not rendered; BSB makes the man the subject of the that-clause.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render τοῦ ἀναβλέψαντος ("of the one who had received his sight") after his parents.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds still; the Greek has no word for it.

9:19.sourceText: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτοὺς λέγοντες Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς ὑμῶν, ὃν ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι τυφλὸς ἐγεννήθη; πῶς οὖν βλέπει ἄρτι;
9:19.targetText: and asked, “Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? So how is it that he can now see?”

groups.note: The relative ὅν ("whom") is rendered the one.

unmappedSource.reason: The object αὐτούς ("them") is not rendered.
The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is not rendered; English introduces the question directly.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
ὅτι ("that") is left implicit in English (you say was born blind).

unmappedTarget.reason: English expands How into "how is it that"; the Greek has only πῶς.

9:20.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπαν Οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς ἡμῶν καὶ ὅτι τυφλὸς ἐγεννήθη·
9:20.targetText: His parents answered, “We know he is our son, and we know he was born blind.

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθησαν … καὶ εἶπαν ("answered and said") is rendered by the one verb answered.
Οἴδαμεν ("we know") is understood again with the second ὅτι clause; BSB repeats it.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render οὖν ("so") here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
ὅτι ("that") is left implicit in English (we know he is …).

9:21.sourceText: πῶς δὲ νῦν βλέπει οὐκ οἴδαμεν, ἢ τίς ἤνοιξεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἡμεῖς οὐκ οἴδαμεν· αὐτὸν ἐρωτήσατε, ἡλικίαν ἔχει, αὐτὸς περὶ ἑαυτοῦ λαλήσει.
9:21.targetText: But how he can now see or who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him. He is old enough to speak for himself.”

groups.note: ἡλικίαν ἔχει ("he has age") is rendered is old enough.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek says οὐκ οἴδαμεν ("we do not know") after each question; BSB joins the questions and says it once.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:22.sourceText: ταῦτα εἶπαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἐφοβοῦντο τοὺς Ἰουδαίους· ἤδη γὰρ συνετέθειντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἵνα ἐάν τις αὐτὸν ὁμολογήσῃ Χριστόν, ἀποσυνάγωγος γένηται.
9:22.targetText: His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews. For the Jews had already determined that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.

groups.note: ἐάν τις ("if anyone") is rendered anyone who.
αὐτόν ("him") is rendered by the name Jesus.
Χριστόν is the predicate of confessed; English marks it with as.
ἀποσυνάγωγος is one Greek adjective, "expelled from the synagogue".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an article before Christ; Χριστόν has none.

9:23.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο οἱ γονεῖς αὐτοῦ εἶπαν ὅτι Ἡλικίαν ἔχει, αὐτὸν ἐπερωτήσατε.
9:23.targetText: That was why his parents said, “He is old enough. Ask him.”

groups.note: διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered That was why.
ἡλικίαν ἔχει ("he has age") is rendered He is old enough.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The ὅτι introducing the quotation is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in "That was why".

9:24.sourceText: Ἐφώνησαν οὖν τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐκ δευτέρου ὃς ἦν τυφλὸς, καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Δὸς δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ· ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.
9:24.targetText: So a second time they called for the man who had been blind and said, “Give glory to God! We know that this man is a sinner.”

groups.note: ἐκ δευτέρου ("from a second [time]") is rendered a second time.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:25.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη οὖν ἐκεῖνος Εἰ ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν οὐκ οἶδα· ἓν οἶδα, ὅτι τυφλὸς ὢν ἄρτι βλέπω.
9:25.targetText: He answered, “Whether He is a sinner I do not know. There is one thing I do know: I was blind, but now I see!”

groups.note: The participle ὤν ("being") is rendered I was.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render οὖν ("so") here.
ὅτι ("that") is replaced by a colon in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a presentational frame before one thing.
English adds but to join the participle clause ("being blind") to the main verb.

9:26.sourceText: εἶπαν οὖν αὐτῷ Τί ἐποίησέν σοι; πῶς ἤνοιξέν σου τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς;

groups.note: BSB's Greek text has a different form of this verb here, with the same meaning.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render οὖν ("so") here.
The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:27.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς Εἶπον ὑμῖν ἤδη καὶ οὐκ ἠκούσατε· τί πάλιν θέλετε ἀκούειν; μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς θέλετε αὐτοῦ μαθηταὶ γενέσθαι;

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτοῖς ("to them") is not rendered.
μή only marks a question expecting the answer no; English has a plain question.

9:28.sourceText: καὶ ἐλοιδόρησαν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπαν Σὺ μαθητὴς εἶ ἐκείνου, ἡμεῖς δὲ τοῦ Μωϋσέως ἐσμὲν μαθηταί·

groups.note: BSB's Greek text has a different form of this verb here, with the same meaning.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ ("but") here; it uses a semicolon.

9:29.sourceText: ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν ὅτι Μωϋσεῖ λελάληκεν ὁ Θεός, τοῦτον δὲ οὐκ οἴδαμεν πόθεν ἐστίν.

τὸ θαυμαστόν ("the remarkable thing") is rendered remarkable.
πόθεν means "from where".

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτοῖς ("to them") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:31.sourceText: οἴδαμεν ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἀκούει, ἀλλ’ ἐάν τις θεοσεβὴς ᾖ καὶ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιῇ, τούτου ἀκούει.

9:32.sourceText: ἐκ τοῦ αἰῶνος οὐκ ἠκούσθη ὅτι ἠνέῳξέν τις ὀφθαλμοὺς τυφλοῦ γεγεννημένου·
9:32.targetText: Never before has anyone heard of opening the eyes of a man born blind.

groups.note: ἐκ τοῦ αἰῶνος ("from the age", since time began) is rendered before.
τις ("someone") is the one who opens in Greek; BSB makes anyone the subject of heard.
The participle γεγεννημένου ("of one born") is rendered of a man born.

unmappedSource.reason: ὅτι ("that") is absorbed in English heard of opening.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an article before eyes; ὀφθαλμούς has none.

9:33.sourceText: εἰ μὴ ἦν οὗτος παρὰ Θεοῦ, οὐκ ἠδύνατο ποιεῖν οὐδέν.

9:34.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ἐν ἁμαρτίαις σὺ ἐγεννήθης ὅλος, καὶ σὺ διδάσκεις ἡμᾶς; καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω.

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθησαν … καὶ εἶπαν ("answered and said") is rendered by the one verb replied.
ἁμαρτίαις is plural ("sins").
ὅλος ("wholly, entirely") is rendered utter.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to him") is not rendered.

9:35.sourceText: Ἤκουσεν Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω, καὶ εὑρὼν αὐτὸν εἶπεν Σὺ πιστεύεις εἰς τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

9:36.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη ἐκεῖνος καὶ εἶπεν Καὶ τίς ἐστιν, Κύριε, ἵνα πιστεύσω εἰς αὐτόν;

9:37.sourceText: εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Καὶ ἑώρακας αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ λαλῶν μετὰ σοῦ ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν.

9:38.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἔφη Πιστεύω, Κύριε· καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτῷ.

9:39.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰς κρίμα ἐγὼ εἰς τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον ἦλθον, ἵνα οἱ μὴ βλέποντες βλέπωσιν καὶ οἱ βλέποντες τυφλοὶ γένωνται.

9:40.sourceText: ἤκουσαν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων ταῦτα οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄντες, καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Μὴ καὶ ἡμεῖς τυφλοί ἐσμεν;

9:41.sourceText: εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰ τυφλοὶ ἦτε, οὐκ ἂν εἴχετε ἁμαρτίαν· νῦν δὲ λέγετε ὅτι Βλέπομεν· ἡ ἁμαρτία ὑμῶν μένει.
9:41.targetText: “If you were blind,” Jesus replied, “you would not be guilty of sin. But since you claim you can see, your guilt remains.”

groups.note: εἴχετε ἁμαρτίαν ("you would have sin") is rendered be guilty of sin.
νῦν ("now") is used in its logical sense, "as it is", and rendered since.
ἁμαρτία ("sin") is rendered guilt here.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτοῖς ("to them") is not rendered.
